title: Adopt the shared wiki contract: repo-local surfaces, retrieval, and dispatch readiness
summary: Tracker for the IN-0001 adoption work. Root AGENTS.md may not exist yet in a freshly bootstrapped repo, so the orchestrator must dispatch the mandatory worker-owned implementation slice WK-0001#SLICE-001 (write_scope ["AGENTS.md"]) to populate or adapt it; an empty AGENTS.md does not satisfy the slice. That implementation delivery receives its automatic mandatory slice-level findings-only review before integration. Bootstrap also seeds the distinct WK-0001#SLICE-002 terminal whole-WK findings-only review required before forge handoff. That terminal review uses only candidate-portable inspection available in the exact detached candidate. The coordinator separately runs lint, adoption verification, graph-impact, dispatch-readiness, and launcher/setup checks from the configured repository root; those checks are not terminal-review commands or findings criteria. Retiring the obsolete adoption-verification review unit removed a separate readiness unit, not either review boundary.
scope: Bring the consuming repo up to the shared wiki/agent contract by dispatching the mandatory worker-owned implementation slice WK-0001#SLICE-001 (write_scope ["AGENTS.md"]) to populate or adapt canonical root AGENTS.md. The orchestrator must not write root `AGENTS.md` directly (orchestrator write scope does not include the repo root) and must not skip authoring it, and an empty AGENTS.md does not satisfy the work. WK-0001#SLICE-001 receives its automatic mandatory findings-only review of the implementation delivery before integration. After SLICE-001, the explicit seeded WK-0001#SLICE-002 reviews only candidate-portable facts in the exact detached terminal candidate against its launcher-bound base: the exact candidate diff, root AGENTS.md, canonical seeded contracts visible in the candidate, placeholder removal, repository adaptation, and factual capability and canonical-layer claims. It is a separate findings-only review boundary with no write or publication authority. The coordinator runs lint, adoption verification, graph-impact, dispatch-readiness, and launcher/setup checks from the configured repository root. These coordinator-only checks are not terminal-review commands or findings criteria and never substitute for either findings-only review. The worker derives repo-specific guidance from wiki/templates/AGENTS.md.boilerplate.md, preserves positively known adopted surfaces, and removes unsupported claims. Dispatch implementation only through scoped `WK-*` slices; proceed once required coordinator checks pass. The Claude @AGENTS.md bridge remains setup context and is not an independent policy source.
out_of_scope: Do not modify the shared agent-chassis packages, do not edit global MCP client config, do not have the orchestrator write root AGENTS.md directly (dispatch the seeded worker-owned slice `WK-0001#SLICE-001` with write_scope ["AGENTS.md"] via the structured MCP dispatch route instead), do not treat the explicit terminal review as adoption verification or as publication, integration, merge, or handoff authority, and do not rerun coordinator-only lint, adoption verification, graph-impact, dispatch-readiness, or launcher/setup checks during terminal review. Missing gitignored, cached, generated, or empty setup surfaces in the exact detached candidate are not terminal-review findings, including `.agent-launch/`, `wiki/.wiki-mcp.json`, `.cache/wiki-search/`, `docs/`, and empty wiki directories. Do not launch the seeded orchestrator while adoption verification reports missing or invalid launcher config (a missing root AGENTS.md alone is advisory and does not block), do not assign a worker to edit or recreate the bootstrap-generated wiki/.wiki-mcp.json (bootstrap owns it as gitignored local metadata), do not assign a worker to author or customize a repo-local adoption guide (the adoption guide is the single package-owned document shipped with @agent-chassis/core and this record is the repository's adoption authority), do not assign a worker to author agent-launch.toml (package/bootstrap first-run guidance supplies the operator copy/init-config step), and note that bootstrap seeding alone does not make the repo agent-operable.

criteria: Root AGENTS.md may not exist yet in a freshly bootstrapped repo.

Candidate-portable inspection in the exact detached candidate is limited to the exact candidate diff, root AGENTS.md content, canonical seeded contracts visible in the candidate, placeholder removal, repository adaptation, and factual capability and canonical-layer claims.

The coordinator runs lint, adoption verification, graph-impact, dispatch-readiness, and launcher/setup checks from the configured repository root, recording a specific structured blocker per non-pass check. These coordinator-only checks are not terminal-review commands or findings criteria.

Root AGENTS.md is authored/adapted as the primary adoption deliverable via the seeded worker-owned implementation slice `WK-0001#SLICE-001` (write_scope ["AGENTS.md"]), dispatched through the structured MCP dispatch route (never written directly by the orchestrator); the result is repo-adapted rather than a bootstrap-generated placeholder. It may be absent immediately after bootstrap, and a transiently-missing root AGENTS.md does not by itself flip the adoption-verify verdict to blocked, but authoring it remains required adoption work, not optional. The orchestrator must not skip authoring it.

`WK-0001#SLICE-001` remains mandatory worker-owned implementation work that receives a mandatory findings-only review after implementation; that review is required before the slice is treated as done and is never satisfied by the coordinator-owned read-only adoption verification.

`WK-0001#SLICE-002` is the distinct explicit terminal whole-WK findings-only review unit required after the implementation slice and before forge handoff; it reviews only candidate-portable facts in the launcher-owned exact candidate against its bound base with empty write scope and grants no publication, integration, merge, or handoff authority.

The seed tells the agent/operator to run `npx agent-chassis setup`, review/adapt `wiki/templates/AGENTS.md.boilerplate.md` into root `AGENTS.md`, rerun `npx wiki adoption verify --dir "$PWD" --json`, and proceed only after required checks pass.

agent-launch.toml exists as operator-supplied first-run launcher config with explicit model defaults for orchestrator, worker, reviewer, and redteam; the coordinator-owned read-only verification confirms the bootstrap-generated wiki/.wiki-mcp.json (schema wiki-mcp-workspace.v1, a resolved current.root, and a repo-derived current.alias), not authored or edited by bootstrap.
The coordinator runs `npx -p @agent-chassis/wiki-cli wiki adoption verify --dir "$PWD" --json` as read-only verification; the repo is not claimed agent-operable unless the verdict is ready.
The Claude @AGENTS.md bridge is setup context only and CLAUDE.md is not an independent policy source.
The boilerplate is a helper template, not current-session operating authority; the orchestrator write scope does not include the repo root.
validation: Coordinator-only; run from the configured repository root; not a terminal-review command or findings criterion: npx -p @agent-chassis/wiki-cli wiki lint --dir "$PWD"

slices.title: Populate or adapt repo-local AGENTS.md
slices.summary: Populate or adapt the consuming repo's root AGENTS.md by deriving the seeded boilerplate helper into repo-specific operating guidance; an empty AGENTS.md does not satisfy this slice. This is the primary adoption deliverable; the orchestrator dispatches this worker slice through the structured MCP dispatch route and never writes the repo root directly. Like every implementation slice, its delivery receives an automatic mandatory slice-level findings-only review before integration; the separate seeded SLICE-002 later reviews the terminal whole-WK candidate.
slices.scope: Populate or adapt root `AGENTS.md` by deriving it from `wiki/templates/AGENTS.md.boilerplate.md`: replace the `[repo-name]` placeholder, adapt each section to this repo's real structured tools, retrieval surfaces, and canonical layers, preserve an accurate positive inventory of adopted repository surfaces, and remove or qualify only claims this repo has not adopted. Bootstrap establishes canonical wiki/work-record coordination and structured wiki MCP capability; preserve those positive facts instead of inferring they are absent because confined worktree visibility omits local setup artifacts. The authored file must be repo-specific operating authority, not a blind copy of the helper, and an empty `AGENTS.md` does not satisfy this slice. The write happens only within this worker slice's write_scope (`AGENTS.md`); the orchestrator must not write the repo root directly. This implementation delivery receives its automatic mandatory slice-level findings-only review before integration. The explicit SLICE-002 terminal whole-WK review is a later, distinct boundary. Coordinator-owned read-only adoption verification is separate work and never stands in for either review.
slices.out_of_scope: Do not copy the boilerplate verbatim, do not leave the `[repo-name]` placeholder or any other bracketed placeholder, do not remove positively known bootstrap-established wiki/work-record or structured wiki MCP surfaces merely because gitignored, cached, generated, or empty setup artifacts are outside the confined worktree, do not claim unsupported tools/MCP/code-index capabilities or canonical layers, do not claim a populated `docs/` tree or any other surface not guaranteed by the seed without repository evidence, and do not edit shared agent-chassis package source or any file outside `AGENTS.md`.

criteria: Root `AGENTS.md` exists at the repo root, derived from `wiki/templates/AGENTS.md.boilerplate.md` and adapted to this repo rather than copied verbatim.
No `[repo-name]` placeholder or any other bracketed placeholder remains in the authored `AGENTS.md`.

Unsupported tool, MCP, and canonical-layer claims carried by the boilerplate are removed or qualified, so every structured tool, MCP capability, and canonical layer named in `AGENTS.md` is actually supported by this repo.

`AGENTS.md` contains an accurate positive inventory of adopted repository surfaces and preserves the bootstrap-established canonical wiki/work-record coordination and structured wiki MCP capability; absence of gitignored, cached, generated, or empty setup artifacts from the confined worktree is not evidence that those adopted surfaces are unsupported.
`AGENTS.md` does not claim a populated `docs/` tree or any other repository surface not guaranteed by the seed unless repository evidence positively establishes it.
`AGENTS.md` reads as repo-specific operating authority, not a blind copy of the helper template.

The delivered `AGENTS.md` receives its automatic mandatory slice-level findings-only review before this slice is treated as done and integrated; that implementation-delivery review is distinct from the explicit `SLICE-002` terminal whole-WK review and is never satisfied by coordinator-owned read-only adoption verification.

slices.title: Review the exact terminal WK-0001 candidate

criteria: Perform a findings-only review in which launcher-owned C/B/W and exact-candidate authority are authoritative, and review the exact terminal WK-0001 candidate C against its launcher-bound base B.

Review only candidate-portable facts: the exact candidate diff, root `AGENTS.md` content (including whether it is nonempty), canonical seeded contracts visible in the candidate, placeholder removal, repository adaptation, and whether capability and canonical-layer claims are factual.

Do not rerun coordinator-only lint, adoption verification, graph-impact, dispatch-readiness, or launcher/setup checks; those checks run from the configured repository root and are outside terminal-review findings criteria.

Do not report findings based on absent gitignored, cached, generated, or empty setup surfaces, including `.agent-launch/`, `wiki/.wiki-mcp.json`, `.cache/wiki-search/`, `docs/`, and empty wiki directories.
Change nothing and grant no publication, integration, merge, or forge-handoff authority; report findings only.
validation: Inspect the launcher-bound B..C diff and the declared candidate surfaces, then return only findings for the exact candidate.
